items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I’d be working opposite Coltrane. I played with Johnny Hartman way before McCoy and Trane... See it would be three bands. John Coltrane Quartet, Benny Carter Trio with Harold Mabern...

ctx.x: So one of my dearest friends from Chicago named John Neeley, rest his soul, he said why don’t you come by and sit in with Gates we called him. Lionel Hampton called him, “Hey Gates, come on Gates.” You know. So I went by and he introduced me to — and the Metropole was like a long bar, it was long and the band was spread out. You know it wasn’t too wide, just long. So John Neeley introduced me and said, “Hey this is Harold Mabern, he’s from Chicago, can he sit in?” And he said, “Yeah, Gates, you want to play…

So I stayed with the band for a whole year, because, like I said, but at some point I was getting a little tired because I wanted to really play, that’s why I was in New York. I said a big band was one thing but I’m not getting that many solos.
